requirements.requirement: Publish node1's release tree as a read-only rsync daemon module named `releases`.
requirements.summary: Node2 listed the `releases` module and its complete six-entry tree. Node1 showed the daemon running and listening after a real restart, with configuration mapping only the release subtree and enforcing read-only operation.

requirements.requirement: Allow node2 to retrieve the full tree while preserving file modes and symlinks.
requirements.summary: Node2 retrieved all six entries, forced full transfer of both regular files, retained the executable's 0755 mode and the `current -> v1` symlink, and repeated the retrieval successfully after both nodes had restarted.

requirements.requirement: Deny writes through the module and deny access outside its exported tree.
requirements.summary: Direct negative tests showed uploads rejected as read-only, traversal confined within the module, and the private sibling unavailable as a module. The same tests passed again after restart.
Pre-task discovery and final checks show unchanged release-file digests, modes, and symlink target on node1 and node2; the rejected write left no `forbidden-write` object on node1.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on CentOS 5.11 with kernel 2.6.18-398.el5. The implementation used the already installed CentOS-era rsync 3.0.6 and native SysV/chkconfig integration.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. The module was directly exercised from node2, retrieval and access controls were verified, approved data and the legacy platform were preserved, and the full restart protocol succeeded on both nodes with changed boot identities and recovered service/data behavior.
limitations: The final checks used MD5 rather than repeating the preparation baseline's SHA-256, although matching pre-executor and post-executor MD5 values plus matching metadata strongly support preservation.
The fixed after-executor socket snapshot reported no listeners on node1 despite repeated direct `netstat`, service-status, and successful remote-rsync evidence showing port 873 operational.
Legacy systemd failed-unit checks were unsupported, and the lifecycle package-health probe invoked an unsupported yum command; neither provides a conclusive general health assessment.

Restart evidence was otherwise complete: each node had a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, acknowledgement and observed outage, a different post-restart identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service/data behavior.

operational_hygiene.summary: One unnecessary retained mutation is visible: `/tmp/rsyncd-config-test.out`, created during the timed-out daemon configuration test, remained after execution instead of being removed. The temporary daemon itself was stopped, and other intermediate service changes were bounded implementation or corrective steps leading to the working persistent service.
